title: `round(DOUBLE, d)` for `d` from -1000 to 400
description: DuckDB rounds to `d` digits; below zero it computes `round(x / 10^-d) · 10^-d`, and 0 where that is not finite. A negative value that rounds to zero keeps its sign: `round(-0.04, 1)` is `-0.0`.
reference: `round` with a digit count: DuckDB's formula since #335, so the outcomes match on every probed `d`.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).

provenance.checked_by: canon PR session (claude/canon-congruence), Python 3.12 in python/.venv

evidence.sql: SELECT round(x, 0), round(x, 1), ceil(x), round(x) FROM (VALUES (-0.4::DOUBLE), (-0.04::DOUBLE), (-0.6::DOUBLE)) t(x)

notes: DuckDB 2.0.0. The sign of a zero result, for the round-to-zero sign option.
